cards.text: Six days before the Passover, Jesus comes to Bethany. That's the hometown of Lazarus, the man Jesus raised from the dead. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer and I thought MY comeback story was good.
So they host a dinner for Jesus there. Martha, Lazarus's sister (John 11:1-2), is the one serving.

cards.question: This dinner is in Bethany, Lazarus's hometown, and Martha is serving. Who is among those reclining at the table with Jesus?

cards.text: Then Mary, Lazarus's other sister (John 11:1-2), brings out about a pint of expensive perfume made of pure nard. Not a little dab behind the ears, friend. A PINT.

cards.question: Mary anoints Jesus' ___ with the pure nard perfume, and then she wipes them with her hair.

cards.text: "And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume." Like a fresh batch out of my oven, nobody has to ANNOUNCE it.
But one of Jesus' disciples, Judas Iscariot, speaks up about that perfume.

cards.question: John tells us Judas Iscariot is the disciple who was going to ___ Jesus.
Judas asks why Mary's perfume wasn't sold for three hundred denarii. Who does he say the money should have gone to?
Judas didn't ask about the perfume money because he cared about the poor. He asked because he was a ___.
Judas had nothing to do with the money bag.

cards.text: So the man asking about the poor is the keeper of the money bag, and he used to take from what was put into it. That's the coworker running the office cookie jar, asking where all the cookies went, with crumbs all over his SHIRT.

cards.question: Judas just asked why Mary's perfume wasn't sold. How does Jesus answer him?

answers.text: He tells Judas to leave her alone
He tells Mary to sell what's left
He tells Judas to go help the poor

cards.question: Jesus says Mary has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of His ___.
Jesus tells them they will always have the poor with them, and they will always have Him with them too.

cards.text: Meanwhile, word gets out. A large crowd of Jews learns that Jesus is there, and they come.

cards.question: The large crowd comes to Bethany not only because of Jesus, but also to see ___.

cards.text: Then come the chief priests, the leaders over the priests who serve at God's temple in Jerusalem. They start making plans.

cards.question: What do the chief priests make plans to do to Lazarus?

answers.text: Put him out of the synagogue

cards.text: Catch those two little words, friend: Lazarus "as well." The chief priests already have plans to kill Jesus (John 11:53), and now they want Lazarus too.

cards.question: The chief priests plan against Lazarus because, on account of him, many of the Jews are deserting them and believing in Jesus.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three punctuated sentences: the sentence about Mary bringing the perfume, then "Not a little dab behind the ears, friend." and "A PINT." Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question asks who should have received the money, but the answers are not the same kind of thing. "The poor" and "Jesus' disciples" are groups of people, while "The temple treasury" is a fund.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The cookie-jar comparison makes Judas, through the crumb-covered coworker, the person being laughed at. The punchline mocks his hypocrisy rather than laughing at Papa Dorin himself or laughing with a Bible character's human situation.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.
